Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center. EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, west Triangle. Quezon City http: f/wn,wu. dilg.gov.ph 09 OPINION No. MAYOR LEODEGARIO A. LABAO, JR. Municipality of Mambusao Province of Capiz Dear Mayor Labao, Jr.: s. zoa This pertains to your letter dated 6 April 2018 requesting this Departrnent for your enlightenment on the payment of salary and Representation and Transportation Allowance (RATA) of former Mayor Jose Alba, Jr. during his preventive suspension. Per your letter, then Mayor Jose Alba, Jr. is demanding for the release of his three (3) month salary and RATA during his preventive suspension from December 2016- February 2017. Hence, you are now seeking this Department's position whether the Municipal Government of Mambusao, Capiz is obliged to pay the said claims, especially the RATA, considering that when the Vice-Mayor (V M) took over the position of the Mayor during the latter's suspension, the said VM has already claimed the RATA intended for the position of Mayor during the 3-month period. At the outset, basic is the rule that salary attaches to the office itself and not to the officer. What salary or emoluments that may be attached by law to a public office do not belong to the incumbent because of any supposed legal duty resulting upon the public to pay for the services rendered by him. On the other hand, on the issue of RATA, an employee whose position is not authorized by law to collect the same but is designated to a position vacated temporarily by the incumbent on account of his leave of absence or other legal reasons, shall be entitled to the regular RATA of the position on reimbursable basis provided he is duly designated by the appointing authorityl. As held in the case of Aldovino, Jr. et.al vs the Commission on Election', preventive suspension is imposed under the Local Government Code when the evidence of guilt is strong and given the gravity of the offense, there is a possibility that the continuance in office of the respondent could influence the witnesses or pose a threat to the safety and integrity of the records and other evidence. Under the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, it is imposed after a valid information (that requires a finding of probable cause) has been filed in court, while under the Ombudsman Act, it is imposed when, in the judgment 1 DILG Legal Opinion No. 20, S. 2018 dated 23 April 2018 2 G.R. No. 184836 dated 23 December 2009

of the Ombudsman, the evidence of guilt is strong; and (a) the charge involves dishonesty, oppression or grave misconduct or neglect in the performance of duty; or (b) the charges would warrant removal from the service; or (c) the respondents continued stay in office may prejudice the case filed against him. Notably, in all cases of preventive suspension, the suspended official is barred from performing the functions of his offce and does not receive salary in the meanwhile, but does not vacate and lose title to his office; loss of office is a consequence that only results upon an eventual finding of guilt or liability. Such non-receipt of full salary or compensation being a necessary consequence of suspension3. However, if former Mayor Alba, Jr. is thereafter acquitted, Section 13 of Republic Act No. 30194 provides that he shall be entitled to reinstatement and to the salaries and benefits which he failed to receive during suspension, unless in the meantime administrative proceedings have been filed against him. With the attached documents herein, although there was a Certification issued by the Sandiganbyanan certifying that the accused in Criminal Case No. SB14CRM0329, Jose Ong Alba, Jr. of Mambusao, Capiz was acquitted per Decision of the Fifth Division dated and promulgated on December 7, 2017, this Department was not informed if there is/are any administrative proceedings that have been filed against him. Thus, if there is/are pending administrative case/s filed against him, in the meantime, his salaries and other benefits should be withheld until the disposition of his administrative case/s. On the payment of the RATA, Local Budget Circular No. 1035 provides that RATA is granted to government officials at monthly standards rates in order to defray representation and transportation expenses while in the actual performance of the duties and responsibilities of their positions. May we note that the government official, in order for him/her to be granted RATA, he/she must be in the actual performance of his duties and responsibilities. In the case of then Mayor Alba, Jr. he was under preventive suspension which necessarily follows that he cannot actually perform his duties and responsibilities as he is barred from performing the functions of his office. To further emphasize, RATA is granted to government officials to cover related representation and transportation expenses incidental to and in connection with the actual performance of function. It may either be commutable or reimbursable. Commutable, if the grant thereof is specifically authorized by law and if funds for its payment are provided for in the agency budget, payment of RATA presupposes actual rendition of services in line with official duties.6 On the other hand, Reimbursable RATA should be duly supported by 3 DILG Legal Opinion No. 19, S. 2016 dated 27 April 2016 4 Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act 5 Amended Rules and Regulations on the Grant of Representation and Transportation Allowances. Sec. 317, Article 8, Chapter 5, Volume 1, Government Accounting and Auditing Manual (GAAM)

receipts or by a certificate to the effect that the expenses had been incurred in accordance with the purpose for which the allowance is granted7. Accordingly, this level believes that, upon lifting of the preventive suspension order against former Mayor Alba, Jr., and assuming that there is no administrative proceedings filed against him, he is entitled to his salaries which he failed to receive during his suspension but not to the RATA. CC: We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Very truly yours, By Autho of the Secretary: AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary Atty. Anthony C. Nuyda Regional Director DILG-Region VI OVestern Visayas) 7 Sec. 286, Article 1, Chapter 5, Volume 1, Government Accounting and Auditing Manual (GAAM)
